checks.claim: OC0: Q is well defined on full real H1 with values in the actual H_sp, independent of the sequence and continuous, with <Q(f),Q(h)>=B_Gamma(f^2,h^2) in (3)-(4).
checks.reason: For smooth compact f_n,f_l, f_n^2-f_l^2=(f_n-f_l)(f_n+f_l) is a test, and its norm is the physical C4 in (3). Bridge (15) with R_sp=R0 bounds it by R_sp N(f_n-f_l)^2 N(f_n+f_l)^2. N is continuous and N<=H1 norm, so the squares are Cauchy. Interlacing gives independence. Joint C4 continuity passes the pairing to the limit and gives the physical (4). The limiting bound ||Q(f)-Q(h)||^2<=R_sp N(f-h)^2 N(f+h)^2 gives continuity. No Linfinity embedding or density of Gamma enters.

checks.reason: Strong measurability follows from composing a continuous map with a separably valued strongly measurable field. Unit mass gives N(g_s)^4=b_s^(alpha/2), and concavity on the unit interval gives the bound R_sp T^(alpha/2). PB(20) extends the identity to all L2(I;H_sp). Combined with (4), and with Section5 of the bridge for joint measurability, this gives the raw K integral, not K_star or an abstract substitute.

checks.claim: OC0: mixed pairing (7)-(8) with smooth Psi, using the pointwise product chi Psi_t and C4(chi,Psi_t,f,f).
checks.reason: Psi_t=chi Psi_t pointwise, with one compact chi equal to 1 on the common spatial support. Hence B(Psi_t,f_n^2)=C4(chi,Psi_t,f_n,f_n), and C4 continuity on H1 passes it to the limit. Polarizing PB(20) gives the time double integral, which Schur and L2 CS make absolutely integrable. Evenness gives B(Psi_t,f^2)=int f^2 (Gamma*Psi_t). Tonelli on nonnegative K, Psi, g^2 and Gamma gives int int h_s g_s^2, finite because h<=H and g has unit mass. Hilbert CS with PB(22) and (6) gives sqrt(v_Psi A(g)).
